title: Billing, Invoicing & Revenue Recognition

toc.text: Billing vs recognition: the two clocks
Hands-on walkthrough: build a schedule and recognize over time

html:
Billing is where the money stops being a number on a contract and starts becoming cash, and revenue recognition is the discipline that decides when that cash is allowed to count as revenue. This phase closes the quote-to-cash loop. In the academy model it owns two of your hardest-working objects and two services: Revenue_Schedule__c with BillingScheduleService and RevenueRecognitionService. It also maps directly to exam content — the Revenue Cloud Consultant blueprint carries Invoice Management at 7%, and ASC 606 / IFRS 15 mechanics are the heart of the recognition questions.

This guide explains the billing schedule, invoicing, credit memos, the five-step ASC 606 / IFRS 15 model, and the four recognition methods used across CPQ and Revenue Cloud — Straight Line, Milestone, Percent Complete, and Immediate.

Learning objectives

  • Explain the difference between billing (cash/invoice timing) and revenue recognition (financial statement timing).
  • Build billing schedules from fulfilled subscription assets with BillingScheduleService.
  • Describe invoicing and credit-memo flows and how they write back to the invoice-management domain.
  • State the ASC 606 / IFRS 15 five-step model from contract identification to recognition.
  • Apply the four recognition methods — Immediate, Straight Line, Milestone, Percent Complete — and pick the right one per product.
  • Model recognition on the Revenue_Schedule__c object and its status lifecycle.
  • Recognize revenue over time with RevenueRecognitionService and validate the math with SOQL.
  • Explain how Revenue Cloud / RLM automates the same model on the core platform.

Billing vs recognition: the two clocks

Billing and recognition are deliberately different clocks. Billing answers "when do we send an invoice and collect cash?" Recognition answers "when do we record the revenue on the income statement?". Under accrual accounting these diverge on purpose — a 12-month license billed annually on day 1 may be recognized evenly across the 12 months.

ClockDrivesTypical trigger
BillingCash and the invoiceAsset start date, payment terms
Revenue recognitionIncome statementPerformance obligation satisfied

The academy model keeps the two apart: a Revenue_Schedule__c record carries both the billing-facing and the recognition-facing data (amount, recognized to date, recognition date, method, period, status), and each method computes how the Amount__c is released over the schedule period.

💡
Tip: Never let cash receipts move the revenue timeline. Billing customers early should accelerate cash, never revenue, unless the obligation is genuinely satisfied.

Building a billing schedule

The schedule is the rhythm section of the lifecycle. Once an order is fulfilled and its subscription asset exists, BillingScheduleService turns it into a set of periods — each period is a scheduled invoice event. For a 12-month annual-upfront deal you get one billing line; for a monthly deal you get twelve.

The academy Revenue_Schedule__c links every money event to its origin, so any report can trace quote → contract → order → account:

FieldMeaning
Quote__cSource quote
Contract__cMaster agreement (amended terms win)
Order__cFulfilled order that generated the asset
Account__cCustomer
Amount__cBilled or recognized amount for the period
Recognized_Amount__cAmount recognized so far against Amount__c
Recognition_Date__cWhen the method says revenue lands
Recognition_Method__cImmediate / Straight Line / Milestone / Percent Complete
Period__cThe period this schedule line covers
Status__cOpen / Recognized / Deferred / Completed
soql
SELECT Account__c, Order__c, Contract__c, Period__c, Amount__c,
       Recognized_Amount__c, Recognition_Method__c, Status__c
FROM Revenue_Schedule__c
WHERE Order__r.Name = 'ORD-SUB-001'
ORDER BY Period__c

Invoicing and credit memos

Invoicing consumes the schedule: each due period produces an invoice (in legacy CPQ, blng__Invoice__c; in Revenue Cloud, invoices and invoice lines on the core data model). Invoices record what was billed and when. Credit memos are the reverse — they cancel or reduce invoiced amounts, whether from an amendment removing a module or a dispute victory.

Object / eventEffect
Invoice issuedCreates an accounts-receivable entry, unlocks cash collection
Partial paymentAR reduces, recognized revenue untouched
Credit memoReverses billable value; recognition recalculated only if the obligation actually shrank
Amendment mid-termNew prorated billing lines; old schedule periods cancelled

Invoice management is its own exam domain (7% of Revenue Cloud Consultant), and the practical rule is symmetrical with the contract rule: never hand-edit a billed amount; let amendments and credit memos do the mutation so the audit trail stays whole.

ASC 606 / IFRS 15: the five-step model

The recognition geometry is dictated by the revenue standards. Both ASC 606 (US GAAP) and IFRS 15 (international) describe the same five steps — they are worded differently, but the model is one:

  1. Identify the contract with the customer — an agreement creating enforceable rights and payment obligations. In the academy model: the Mastered contract.
  2. Identify the performance obligations — the distinct goods or services promised. Each meaningful deliverable in the quote/contract lines.
  3. Determine the transaction price — the total consideration expected. Post-discount total from the quote (Total_ARR__c × term, net of discounts).
  4. Allocate the transaction price to the obligations — split the total across obligations, typically by their standalone selling price (SSP). This is where a hardware-plus-subscription bundle gets its 20/80 split.
  5. Recognize revenue when (or as) each obligation is satisfied — at a point in time for HW, over time for subscriptions — which is exactly what the four recognition methods implement.
StepAcademy object/fieldQuestion it answers
1 ContractContract (CPQ_Contract_Status__c = Mastered)Do we have an enforceable deal?
2 ObligationsQuote/Contract linesWhat did we promise?
3 Transaction priceQuote Total_ARR__c net of discountHow much total?
4 AllocationAllocated line values (SSP basis)How much per promise?
5 RecognitionRevenue_Schedule__c + methodWhen does it become revenue?

The exam reward is in step 5: recognize a point-in-time deliverable immediately, and a recurring obligation over time — but never before it is earned.

The four recognition methods

The academy data model exposes Recognition_Method__c and the RevenueRecognitionService implements the arithmetic. Match the method to the obligation:

MethodMeaningTypical product
ImmediateRecognize the full amount at the point the obligation is satisfiedHardware, one-time services, SPLA-style point sale
Straight LineRecognize evenly over the term's periodsSubscriptions: 12 months, 1/12 per month
MilestoneRecognize when agreed milestones are reachedImplementation: on kickoff, on go-live
Percent CompleteRecognize proportional to completionLong services: 40% complete → 40% recognized
apex
// RevenueRecognitionService: straight-line release for one schedule line
public class RevenueRecognitionService {
    public static Decimal straightLinePortion(Revenue_Schedule__c line) {
        return line.Amount__c / line.PeriodsRemaining__c; // simplified; uses period math
    }
}

The honest math: Immediate journals the full amount on the recognition date; Straight Line divides Amount__c by the number of periods and releases installments each period; Milestone releases the discrete value when Recognition_Date__c hits; Percent Complete releases Amount__c × %Complete. Recognized_Amount__c accumulates so the schedule status can flip to Recognized only when Recognized_Amount__c == Amount__c.

text
Straight Line, $12,000 / 12 months:
  P1 1,000 | P2 1,000 | ... | P12 1,000   -> Recognized_Amount__c reaches 12,000

Milestone, $10,000 implementation:
  Kickoff  -> 4,000 recognized
  Go-live  -> 6,000 recognized
💡
Tip: Deferred revenue is what hangs between billed and recognized. A schedule line with Status__c = Deferred is a liability, not revenue — confuse the two and the financial statements will fight you.

Automating recognition and deferred revenue

Recognition automation is a scheduled job: on the right day every period that comes due gets its journal entry, Recognized_Amount__c ticks up, and the line lands in Recognized. The academy pattern uses RevenueRecognitionService driven by a batch/cron trigger that reads Recognition_Date__c and the method:

apex
List<Revenue_Schedule__c> due = [
    SELECT Id, Amount__c, Recognized_Amount__c, Recognition_Method__c
    FROM Revenue_Schedule__c
    WHERE Recognition_Date__c <= TODAY
      AND Status__c NOT IN ('Recognized','Cancelled')
];

for (Revenue_Schedule__c line : due) {
    line.Recognized_Amount__c = RevenueRecognitionService.release(line);
    line.Status__c = (line.Recognized_Amount__c == line.Amount__c)
        ? 'Recognized'
        : 'Partially Recognized';
}
update due;

The "recognized when fully recognized" guard prevents clocking a partial method as done — the status is derived from math, not from the calendar. Revenue Cloud / RLM automates this same model with revenue schedules, revenue contracts, and deferred-revenue seats on the core platform, which is why analysts with the Revenue Cloud Consultant cert are expected to explain both the legacy schedule and the next-gen model.

Hands-on walkthrough: build a schedule and recognize over time

Use the academy data model with BillingScheduleService and RevenueRecognitionService.

  1. Start from the fulfilled subscription order (ORD-SUB-001) and its asset from the Orders phase, Total_ARR__c = 24,000 on an annual subscription.
  2. Call BillingScheduleService to generate the schedule — monthly periods across the term:
apex
List<Revenue_Schedule__c> schedule =
    BillingScheduleService.build(
        quoteId, contractId, orderId, accountId,
        amount, periods, 'Straight Line'
    );
  1. Confirm 12 Revenue_Schedule__c lines, each Amount__c = 2,000, method Straight Line, Period__c sequential, Status__c = Deferred.
  2. Manually run the batch that recognizes due periods and confirm month 1 becomes Recognized with Recognized_Amount__c = 2,000.
soql
SELECT Period__c, Amount__c, Recognized_Amount__c, Status__c
FROM Revenue_Schedule__c
WHERE Order__r.Name = 'ORD-SUB-001' AND Recognition_Method__c = 'Straight Line'
ORDER BY Period__c LIMIT 3
  1. Create a second product line with Recognition_Method__c = 'Immediate' worth $5,000 and confirm it recognizes in full on its date, Recognized_Amount__c = 5,000, in one step.
  2. Add a Milestone implementation line: two milestones ($4,000 on kickoff, $6,000 on go-live). Recognize the first milestone and confirm Status__c stays Partially Recognized until the second is released.
  3. Add a Percent Complete service line of $10,000, post 40% completion, and confirm recognition releases $4,000.
  4. Emit an amendment removing one monthly subscription period and confirm the affected schedule lines are cancelled and the amended term drives the remaining recognition — never the original snapshot.

Common pitfalls

  • Treating billing as recognition — cash collected on day one of an annual term is billed, not earned; the schedule keeps the deferral honest.
  • Recognizing on the wrong date — using an invoice date instead of Recognition_Date__c will front-load revenue and fail controls.
  • Forgetting the status guard — a batch job that flips lines to Recognized without checking Recognized_Amount__c == Amount__c breaks partial methods like Milestone.
  • Directly editing Recognized_Amount__c — mutation must go through RevenueRecognitionService so the ledger and the object never drift.
  • Bunching periods together — combining monthly periods into one schedule line makes proration and amendments messy; keep one line per period.
  • Recognition after cancellation — cancelled or amended obligations must reverse out; never keep recognizing a line the contract no longer supports.

Key takeaways

  • Billing (cash/invoice timing) and recognition (financial-statement timing) are separate clocks that the schedule reconciles.
  • Revenue_Schedule__c is the money ledger linking quote, contract, order, and account with every period, amount, and method.
  • ASC 606 / IFRS 15 are the same five steps: contract → obligations → price → allocation → recognition. Learn all five for both exam and practice.
  • Match the method to the obligation: Immediate for point-in-time deliverables, Straight Line for subscriptions, Milestone for staged work, Percent Complete for ongoing services.
  • Release revenue through the service, guard on Recognized_Amount__c, and let Status__c derive from the math — deferred revenue is a liability until it is earned.
  • Revenue Cloud / RLM automates exactly this model on core objects, so the discipline transfers from legacy CPQ to the next-generation platform.
